extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, issuing, and responding to final Office actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings, including panel review procedures, required form paragraphs, timing/extension rules, and signatory authority. Focuses on when a rejection may be made final and how panel review must be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a clear issue before final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a final action is in order, a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To bring prosecution to a speedy conclusion and deal justly with the patent owner and the public, the examiner will twice provide the patent owner with such information and references as may be useful in defining the position of the Office as to unpatentability before the action is made final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision ordering reexamination must identify substantial new questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision ordering reexamination of the patent will contain an identification of the substantial new questions of patentability that the examiner considers to be raised by the cited prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification should make clear the grounds on which reexamination was ordered so the patent owner understands the issues to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office action must consider all submissions and apply relevant grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action should reflect the consideration of any arguments contained in the request, any amendments submitted with a request under 35 U.S.C. 302, any owner’s statement filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.530, and any reply thereto by the requester, and should fully apply all relevant grounds of rejection to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should fully apply relevant grounds of rejection and explicitly account for arguments/amendments/statements made by parties in the initial prosecution materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement/response should fully address outstanding grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement which the patent owner may file under 37 CFR 1.530 and the response to the first Office action should completely respond to and/or amend with a view to avoiding all outstanding grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners are expected to comprehensively respond or amend to remove outstanding grounds; examiners should expect and consider such complete responses when proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Office action generally to be made final using MPEP 706.07(a) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: It is intended that the second Office action in the reexamination proceeding following the decision ordering reexamination will generally be made final. The criteria for making a rejection final in an ex parte reexamination proceeding is analogous to that set forth in MPEP § 706.07(a) for making a rejection final in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both examiner and patent owner should recognize that reexamination may result in final cancellation of claims; use the same substantive standards for finality as in standard applications per MPEP §706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: No right to renew or continue prosecution by refiling or RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner does not have the right to renew or continue the proceedings by refiling under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 37 CFR 1.53(d) or former 37 CFR 1.60 or 1.62, nor by filing a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should not rely on refiling or RCE mechanisms to continue reexamination prosecution; reexamination has its own procedural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete examiner actions and early evidence presentation to avoid prolonged prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete and thorough actions by the examiner coupled with complete responses by the patent owner, including early presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) or 37 CFR 1.132, will go far in avoiding such problems and reaching a desirable early termination of the reexamination prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early submission of evidence (e.g., affidavits or declarations) and thorough work by examiners help resolve issues sooner and may prevent cancellation or protracted proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection must clearly develop and reiterate all outstanding grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the final rejection, all outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed and any grounds or rejection relied on should be reiterated. The grounds of rejection must (in the final rejection) be clearly developed to such an extent that the patent owner may readily judge the advisability of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a single previous Office action already contains a complete statement of a ground, the final rejection may refer to that statement but should also include a rebuttal of any arguments raised in the patent owner’s response. Ensure clarity so owner can assess appeal options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review required during preparation of Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: After an examiner determines the reexamination proceeding is ready for the final Office action, the examiner will set up a panel review conference, as per MPEP § 2271.01, to discuss the issuance of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may prepare the action before or after the conference and revise it as needed. If the conference confirms the preliminary decision to reject/allow, the proposed final Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner with conferees initialing to indicate participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 22.09 and 22.10 conclude final rejection letters with specific timing and extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rejection letter should conclude with one of form paragraphs 22.09 or 22.10. These paragraphs state that the action is made final and set a shortened statutory period for response, and explain that extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply in reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs specify that extensions are governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c), detail filing/fee requirements for extension requests (including timing and sufficiency of cause), and normally insert TWO (2) MONTHS in bracketed response periods. Examiner Notes explain permissible use and necessary bracket insertions (e.g., filing date of amendment). The filing of a timely first response is construed to request a two-month extension, but the response period never exceeds six months from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art cited by patent owner (IDS) may be used and trigger final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted in a prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 37 CFR 1.555 (an IDS filed in a reexamination is construed as a prior art citation) and the submission is not accompanied by a statement similar to that of 37 CFR 1.97(e), the examiner may use the art submitted and make the next Office action final whether or not the claims have been amended, provided that no other new ground of rejection is introduced by the examiner based on the new art not cited in the prior art citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If owner submits prior art without the required statement, it can be used by examiner to make the next OA final; ensure no additional new grounds are relied upon beyond that submitted art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure final OA bears a primary examiner's signature (and conferees' initials where panel review occurred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review at each stage except informal/incomplete-response actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review will be conducted at each stage of the examiner’s examination in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, other than for actions such as notices of informality or incomplete response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters requiring decision outside the examiner’s jurisdiction (e.g., petitions, extensions of time, CRU support staff notices) are not subject to panel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel will consist of three, or more, members, one of whom will be a manager. The second member will be the examiner in charge of the proceeding. The manager may select the third member. The examiner-conferees will be primary examiners, or examiners who are knowledgeable in the technology of the invention claimed in the patent being reexamined and/or who are experienced in reexamination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority of those present should be examiners who were not involved in the examination or issuance of the patent. An 'original' examiner should be chosen only if that examiner is the most knowledgeable in the art or there is some other specific and justifiable reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel process for review and issuance of Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must inform their managers of their intent to issue an Office action. The manager will convene a panel and the members will confer and review the patentability of the claim(s). If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with the two, or more, other conferees initialing the action (as 'conferee') to indicate their participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conferees will initial even if one dissented. If the conference does not confirm the preliminary decision, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and expected outcomes of the conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference will provide a forum to assist the assigned examiner in considering all issues of patentability as well as procedural issues having an impact on patentability. Review by more than one primary examiner should diminish perception that the patent owner can disproportionately influence the examiner in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference should provide comprehensive discussion and a finding for each issue; examiner in charge benefits from multiple perspectives to ensure all matters are appropriately addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and challenge procedure for failure to hold panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the examiner issue an Office action without panel review, the patent owner or the third party requester who wishes to object must promptly file a paper alerting the Office of this fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action or it will not be considered. Failure to hold a panel review, by itself, is not grounds for vacating any Office decision(s) or 'restarting' the reexamination proceeding.
